title: Lyon 2021 §5.2 strip-based variable reduction
description: Lyon 2021 §5.2: Reduce ILP variable count from per-arc to per-strip. A 'strip' = consecutive patches bounded by two traces; arcs along the strip share one variable (consistency Eq.(2) is trivially satisfied within a strip). Section 5.2 bounds total vars by (3/2)·n_traces — paper's ROCKERARM has #Arcs=2742 but #Vars=192, vs our current per-arc formulation that would hand all 2742 to ojAlgo. Without this, IntegerSolver hangs on any real mesh (>~200 arcs). Implementation: build strip equivalence classes from the T-mesh via union-find on opposite-arc pairs in 4-cycle patches, emit one ILP var per class, rewrite consistency constraints (trivial within-class, only cross-class for T-junctions), validity Eq.(3) and layout Eq.(4) constraints rewritten to use class IDs.
definition-of-done: On Hand-30k T-mesh #vars drops from 332 to roughly equal-or-less than (3/2)·n_traces; full Quantization.solve completes in <2s; existing 77/77 quadlayout unit tests still pass.
testing-plan: Add ReducedVarsTest fixture: input a synthetic 4x4 T-mesh patch grid, verify strip count + variable count = (3/2)*n_traces. Hand-30k regression: assert ILP completes in finite time. Use -Dixdar.lyon.measureILPVars to print var count to stdout.
